messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99 > 2.5s for /v1/streaming (p95=450ms p99=2.8s) — triggered by latency-detector at 2026-03-15T09:12:14Z :rotating_light:
alex: saw the alert. paging oncall (pd triggered). any obvious deploys?
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: maria accepted the incident (on-call) — escalation: P1.
maria: on it. quick context: streaming path only or other endpoints?
sam: looks isolated to streaming endpoints and server-side streaming tail. metrics: open streams backlog spiked ~x3 starting 09:11Z.
lee: adding grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood/services/streaming?from=now-15m — p99 spike correlates with dropped connections on ai-runtime-3.
alex: can someone run a quick top-level check: 1) pod restarts 2) queue backlog 3) kvcache missrate?
maria: running checks now:
maria: ```
# pods
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=streaming -o wide
# queue
redis-cli -h redis-streaming BRPOP stream_backlog 0
# kvcache metrics
curl -s http://metrics.internal/kvcache | jq '.streaming | {miss_rate,hit_rate}'
```
chris: logs show repeated stall at the encoder step, `send_chunk` blocking ~1200-1800ms when p99 spikes. snippet:
chris: ```
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z ERROR encoder.go:412 send_chunk timeout=1700ms conn_id=xyz123 msg="blocked on gpu-flush"
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z WARN  runtime.go:289 kvcache-miss model=redwood-rlhf v=3
```
sam: interesting — kvcache-miss around same time but miss rate only +8%. encoder blocking suggests GPU hot spots or scheduling stalls.
lee: checking GPU metrics: ai-runtime-3 GPU util 98%, mem pressure high, context-switch rate elevated. might be a single pod getting overloaded.
amend (maria): mitigation options: 1) scale up streaming deployment (replicas +2) 2) rotate traffic off overloaded instance via router 3) fallback to lower-quant model variant temporarily.
alex: do we have autoscale headroom? Dedicated pool has burst capacity but config says no autoscale for streaming lane without manual command.
maria: proceeding with manual scale first. issuing:
maria: ```
kubectl scale deploy streaming --replicas=6 -n inference
redwood-router set-route-weight --route /v1/streaming --remove-host ai-runtime-3
```
lee: scaling started; pods coming up (2 new pods initializing). router change applied, removing ai-runtime-3 from rotation for streaming.
chris: after ~60s p95 back to ~420ms, p99 down to 900ms. backlog draining. :thumbsup:
alex: good. can we also enable temporary model fallback for long-tail requests (>2s) to reduce GPU pressure? maria?
maria: yes, enabling fallback policy (canary) for 5m window:
maria: ```
redwood-policy apply --name streaming-fallback --if p99>1.5s --action route-to:quantized-small --duration 5m
```
sam: applying now. also flagged an eval regression alert in the console for the quantized-small variant but acceptable for short window.
lee: monitoring: p95 steady ~410ms, p99 ~780ms. connections stable. no new pod restarts.
chris: follow-ups: capture heap/gpu stack from ai-runtime-3 before we bring it back. its logs show repeated kernel enqueue latency spikes.
maria: recorded and archived logs + heapdump: s3://redwood-archives/incidents/6078901234/ — will run `gdb` capture tomorrow if we need deeper.
alex: customer impact: any errors exposed to customers?
sam: error rate for streaming client=0.6% (baseline 0.1%) during spike window; most were 504 timeouts at client side due to long-tail chunking. small subset of high-QPS customers hit transient latency >3s. notifying CS to prep comms.
maria: paging notes: created incident ticket IS-607890 in tracker, assigned infra and runtime owners (lee, chris).
lee: plan to bring ai-runtime-3 back into rotation after 30m and observe. we'll also open a follow-up to enable better autoscale rules for streaming lanes.
chris: TODOs: 1) capture gpu kernel timeline 2) add extra logging around send_chunk duration 3) add alert that ties p99 > 2s + gpu util > 90%
alex: thanks all. we can close this thread once p99 stable for 15m and backlog drained. tagging SRE-runbook-bot for postmortem checklist.
SRE-runbook-bot: Postmortem checklist created: https://pm.redwood/incidents/IS-607890/checklist — assign owner within 24h.
maria: marking as being monitored — will update after 15m stable window.
chris: final check at 09:35Z — p99 610ms, backlog at normal. closing active mitigation.
